To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
graft copolymer of soy protein concentrate was synthesized using ethylmethacrylic acid and ascorbic acid/potassium persulphates as a redox initiator system.
the soy protein concentrate was modified by graft co-plymerization using ethylmethacrylic acid under pressure to enhance its thermal and physico-chemical properties.

the soy protein concentrate can be grafted with ethylethacrylate under pressure using ascorbic/potassium persulphates as redox initiator and grafting reaction conditions were optimized to get 59.5% graft yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the grafting of ethyl methacrylate on soy protein concentrate under pressure to improve its physicochemical properties.
the grafting of soy protein concentrate with EMA to modify its physico-chemical properties.
modification of natural protein by graft co- polymerization to improve its chemical and thermal properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
graft copolymerisation is a very efficient technique to modify the properties of protein.
graft copolymerized soy protein concentrate has better chemical and thermal stability than ungrafted soy protein concentrate.
pressure induced graft coploymerization can be used to modify the chemical and thermal properties of soy protein concentrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
graft copolymerized soy protein concentrate is a potential candidate for use in food industry.
grafting of soy protein with ethylmethacylate has improved its chemical, mechanical and thermal properties.
pressure induced graft copolymers of SPC with EMA can be successfully prepared under optimum reaction conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the grafting process has been optimized for maximum graft yield (60 %) under the reaction conditions of reaction pressure (7.5 psi), reaction time (150 min), solvent (150 ml), initiator ratio (AAc: KPS;1:1.2), pH (8), [EMA]; (1.99 X10 -3 MolL -1 ) and graft yield of 59.5% under the reaction conditions.
the grafting of EMA onto SPC backbone can be used as a method for improving the physico-chemical properties of soy protein concentrate.
SPC is a good substrate for graft polymerization with EMA and it can be further modified for different applications.
